items.reason: Artifact ordering places exploration.md after spec and before progress.
Dashboard artifacts consume the same ordered artifact list.
The orphan check explicitly exempts ExplorationFileName.
Other manifest validation and orphan-markdown refusals remain intact.
ExploreDeclared reads the set-level explore boolean.
Only explicit true enables automatic exploration.
ExplorerOverride uses the shared agents-and-effort directive type.
The guide documents both keys and explicitly distinguishes opt-in from opt-out.
The guide states the shared-seam and dependent-later-task rule.
Shared constants generate the guide, with a validation round-trip test.
The new command invokes an Explorer with task listings, bodies, and available spec.
The prompt requests ownership, seams, invariants, tests, and reading ranges.
The prompt requires anchored claims, approximately one page, and the observed commit.
The Explorer template requests no prior-art research or section.
Successful passes atomically replace the flat exploration.md file.
Exploration has its own captured-run phase and retry-cap accounting.
Manual exploration bypasses both declaration and automatic-exploration configuration.
Failed, timed-out, and interrupted attempts cannot replace the report.
Integration tests invoke exploreResolvedSet directly; none exercises the command through report and captured-run creation.
Implement prompts conditionally receive the existing report’s path and description.
Implement prompt construction passes only the report path, never its contents.
The prompt permits only correcting lines falsified by the current attempt.
The edit boundary explicitly permits the exploration report beside the task file.
The prior-art block remains unchanged, with a byte-comparison assertion.
Assist includes the exploration pointer alongside refinement and recent progress.
Existing absent-report goldens and new present-report goldens cover both prompts.
Exploration is skipped when no AFK task is initially eligible and never reconsidered after a HITL gate unlocks tasks.
An existing report bypasses the Explorer and its spending.
Undeclared sets bypass automatic exploration.
The dedicated work.explore group defaults enabled when absent or unspecified.
Disabled configuration bypasses drain exploration while manual exploration remains available.
Resolution applies CLI overrides before manifest directives, then configuration.
The explore phase explicitly skips human-completed sets.
Report reuse depends on presence without comparing its recorded tree to HEAD.
Whole-drain tests cover absent and existing reports and assert Explorer invocation behavior.
The shared fallback walk retries failures using the standard per-phase cap.
Exhausted exploration stops the drain and derives EXPLORE-FAILED for ready sets without reports.
Parking derives from captured runs and report absence without schema additions.
EXPLORE-FAILED is distinct from the unchanged BLOCKED status.
Ready-set selection and daemon dispatch exclude rows carrying EXPLORE-FAILED.
attendableHITLTaskSets ignores row status and can select a parked set with an open HITL task.
Failure recording occurs once outside the retry loop and includes the phase and reason.
--skip-explore bypasses exploration and permits an explicitly targeted parked set to drain.
A successful manual report or removal of the declaration clears the derived park.
CONTEXT.md adds the stopping status but omits it from the explicit automatic-selection skip list.
Unexplored marks carry their reasons separately and render them as adjacent detail.
ResolveExploreMark returns no mark for undeclared sets.
Refresh resolves exploration once and propagates its fields to all four status surfaces.
Parked rows retain exploration fields through dashboard and work-status rendering.
Reports created manually for undeclared sets receive no detail-view path-and-tree pointer.
The sign-off gate suppresses the exploration pointer when the set has a report but no explore declaration.
Any historical explore run causes parking after report deletion, including successful runs, preventing automatic regeneration.

scores.rationale: Good reuse and broad coverage, but parking, HITL scheduling, undeclared-report visibility, and command integration testing remain incomplete.
